# Behavior principles

A principle holds across the specs. An expectation refines every principle and requirement whose
statement covers it directly, whichever spec the requirement belongs to.

<a id="PRIN-NO-LEAKS"></a>

**Principle PRIN-NO-LEAKS**: The daemon leaves nothing behind

*Refines:* [PRIN-OWNS-ONLY-ITS-OWN](#PRIN-OWNS-ONLY-ITS-OWN) · *Refined by:* [BR-CLEAN-BUILTIN-RULES](network/bridge-networking.md#BR-CLEAN-BUILTIN-RULES), [BR-CLEAN-ISOLATION-CHAIN](network/bridge-networking.md#BR-CLEAN-ISOLATION-CHAIN), [BR-CLEAN-OTHER-BACKEND](network/bridge-networking.md#BR-CLEAN-OTHER-BACKEND), [IPVL-NETIF-NO-PARENT-REMOVED](network/ipvlan-networking.md#IPVL-NETIF-NO-PARENT-REMOVED), [IPVL-NETIF-VLAN-PARENT-REMOVED](network/ipvlan-networking.md#IPVL-NETIF-VLAN-PARENT-REMOVED), [NET-API-CONNECT-FAILED-NO-IFACE](network/network-common.md#NET-API-CONNECT-FAILED-NO-IFACE), [NET-API-CONNECT-FAILED-NOT-LISTED](network/network-common.md#NET-API-CONNECT-FAILED-NOT-LISTED), [NET-API-START-FAILED-ENDPOINT-NOT-LISTED](network/network-common.md#NET-API-START-FAILED-ENDPOINT-NOT-LISTED), [NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-NO-PARENT-REMOVED](network/network-common.md#NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-NO-PARENT-REMOVED), [NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-REMOVED](network/network-common.md#NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-REMOVED), [NET-RESTART-NAMESPACES-REMOVED](network/network-common.md#NET-RESTART-NAMESPACES-REMOVED) · *Violated by:* [BR-CLEAN-BUILTIN-CHAIN-RULES](network/bridge-networking.md#BR-CLEAN-BUILTIN-CHAIN-RULES), [BR-CLEAN-NO-FORWARD-JUMP](network/bridge-networking.md#BR-CLEAN-NO-FORWARD-JUMP), [DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](network/container-dns.md#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE), [NET-API-DISCONNECT-IFACE-LEFT](network/network-common.md#NET-API-DISCONNECT-IFACE-LEFT), [NET-API-FAILED-CONNECT-IFACE-LEFT](network/network-common.md#NET-API-FAILED-CONNECT-IFACE-LEFT)

What the daemon creates for a network, an endpoint, a container, a sandbox or a service does not
outlive that object. Examples are network namespaces, interfaces, firewall rules, kernel state
for encryption and the daemon's records of the object. Nothing of it remains once the object is
gone. After the daemon restarts following a crash, or after an upgrade, nothing that the earlier
daemon created remains unless the daemon still uses it for an object that exists. An operation
on the object that fails leaves nothing of what the operation created.

A request or a daemon setting whose configuration the daemon or a driver cannot apply fails: the
request is refused, or the daemon does not start with that setting. The daemon does not go on
with that configuration ignored, or with another value in its place.

<a id="PRIN-AMBIGUITY-NOT-DESTRUCTIVE"></a>

**Principle PRIN-AMBIGUITY-NOT-DESTRUCTIVE**: A request by an ambiguous name or ID prefix is refused

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAITHFUL](#PRIN-FAITHFUL) · *Refined by:* [NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX](network/network-common.md#NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX), [NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-CLI](network/network-common.md#NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-CLI), [NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX](network/network-common.md#NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX) · *Violated by:* [NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX](network/network-common.md#NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX), [NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-SWARM-PREDEFINED](network/network-common.md#NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-SWARM-PREDEFINED), [NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-SWARM-SCOPED](network/network-common.md#NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-SWARM-SCOPED)

A request names an object by its full ID, then by its name, then by a prefix of its ID, and the
first of these that matches decides. A request whose string matches more than one object at that
rank is refused. The request changes and removes none of the objects that the string matches.

<a id="PRIN-FAIL-FAST"></a>

**Principle PRIN-FAIL-FAST**: A request that cannot succeed is refused as early as it can be

*Refines:* [PRIN-USER-INFORMED](#PRIN-USER-INFORMED) · *Refined by:* [NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID](network/network-common.md#NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID), [NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE](network/network-common.md#NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE), [NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-SUBNET](network/network-common.md#NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-SUBNET) · *Violated by:* [IPVL-OPT-MAC-ADDRESS-UNCHECKED](network/ipvlan-networking.md#IPVL-OPT-MAC-ADDRESS-UNCHECKED), [NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CONNECT-STOPPED](network/network-common.md#NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CONNECT-STOPPED), [NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CTR-CREATE](network/network-common.md#NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CTR-CREATE), [NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-ID](network/network-common.md#NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-ID), [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-UNCHECKED](network/network-common.md#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-UNCHECKED), [NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-UNCHECKED](network/network-common.md#NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-UNCHECKED)

When a request cannot succeed because of what it asks, given the properties that the objects it
names keep for as long as they exist, the daemon refuses it with an error response, at the
earliest request at which the daemon can detect the problem. A request that the daemon accepts
does not leave such a failure to a later request, to the tasks of a service, or to the daemon
log. A failure that depends on state that can change before the later request, such as whether
an object exists, what holds a resource, or the configuration of the daemon or the host, is not
one of these: [*PRIN-WARN-AHEAD*](#PRIN-WARN-AHEAD) covers it.

<a id="PRIN-USER-INFORMED"></a>

**Principle PRIN-USER-INFORMED**: The daemon keeps the user informed

*Refined by:* [PRIN-ERRORS-ACTIONABLE](#PRIN-ERRORS-ACTIONABLE), [PRIN-FAIL-FAST](#PRIN-FAIL-FAST), [PRIN-WARN-AHEAD](#PRIN-WARN-AHEAD)

The daemon keeps the user informed. It reports a problem with a request at the earliest point it
can, in terms the user can act on, and never leaves the user to discover from later behavior
that a request did not do what was asked.

<a id="PRIN-FAITHFUL"></a>

**Principle PRIN-FAITHFUL**: A request does what it asks, or nothing

*Refined by:* [PRIN-AMBIGUITY-NOT-DESTRUCTIVE](#PRIN-AMBIGUITY-NOT-DESTRUCTIVE), [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED), [PRIN-REPEATABLE](#PRIN-REPEATABLE) · *Violated by:* [IPVL-NETIF-VLAN-PARENT-REMOVED-MACVLAN](network/ipvlan-networking.md#IPVL-NETIF-VLAN-PARENT-REMOVED-MACVLAN), [NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-REMOVED-IPVLAN](network/network-common.md#NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-REMOVED-IPVLAN)

The daemon does what a request asks, or nothing. It does not apply something other than what was
asked, act on objects the request did not name unambiguously, or let anything the request does
not control decide the outcome.

<a id="PRIN-OWNS-ONLY-ITS-OWN"></a>

**Principle PRIN-OWNS-ONLY-ITS-OWN**: The daemon manages only what it creates

*Refined by:* [IPVL-NETIF-VLAN-PARENT-KEPT](network/ipvlan-networking.md#IPVL-NETIF-VLAN-PARENT-KEPT), [NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-KEPT](network/network-common.md#NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-KEPT), [PRIN-NO-LEAKS](#PRIN-NO-LEAKS), [REQ-BR-DOCKER-USER-KEPT](network/bridge-networking.md#REQ-BR-DOCKER-USER-KEPT), [REQ-BR-FIREWALLD-ZONE](network/bridge-networking.md#REQ-BR-FIREWALLD-ZONE), [REQ-IPVL-VLAN-PARENT](network/ipvlan-networking.md#REQ-IPVL-VLAN-PARENT) · *Violated by:* [REQ-BR-IP-FORWARDING-DROP](network/bridge-networking.md#REQ-BR-IP-FORWARDING-DROP)

The daemon manages only what it creates. It removes everything it creates once the object it
belongs to is gone, and it leaves alone what it did not create: it does not remove or change it. Where the daemon's own state sits relative to what others add, such as the order of rules in a chain that both use, is not promised, except at an anchor or where users observably rely on it.

<a id="PRIN-NODE-LOCAL"></a>

**Principle PRIN-NODE-LOCAL**: A node-local object is a resource of its node

A network of local scope, like a volume, is a resource of the node that has it. On that node,
whether something uses it depends only on the objects that exist on that node: a Swarm object
that names it, such as a Swarm-scoped network created with `ConfigFrom`, uses it on
a node only while that object has a local attachment there. Whether a Swarm object can use a
node's local resources is for the orchestrator to decide, as it decides where tasks run.

<a id="PRIN-LEAST-ACCESS"></a>

**Principle PRIN-LEAST-ACCESS**: The daemon grants no access the user did not ask for

*Refined by:* [REQ-BR-NO-DIRECT-ROUTING](network/bridge-networking.md#REQ-BR-NO-DIRECT-ROUTING), [REQ-BR-SEPARATE-NETWORKS](network/bridge-networking.md#REQ-BR-SEPARATE-NETWORKS), [REQ-BR-UNPUBLISHED-PORTS](network/bridge-networking.md#REQ-BR-UNPUBLISHED-PORTS), [REQ-DNS-FWD-INTERNAL](network/container-dns.md#REQ-DNS-FWD-INTERNAL), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-SCOPE](network/container-dns.md#REQ-DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-SCOPE), [REQ-NET-INTERNAL-NO-EXTERNAL-ACCESS](network/network-common.md#REQ-NET-INTERNAL-NO-EXTERNAL-ACCESS) · *Violated by:* [REQ-BR-INTERNAL](network/bridge-networking.md#REQ-BR-INTERNAL), [REQ-NET-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-ATTACHMENT](network/network-common.md#REQ-NET-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-ATTACHMENT)

The daemon grants no access the user did not ask for.

<a id="PRIN-STABLE"></a>

**Principle PRIN-STABLE**: What a release does, later minor releases keep doing

*Refined by:* [PRIN-SECURITY-NOT-WEAKENED](#PRIN-SECURITY-NOT-WEAKENED), [REQ-NET-API-BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE](network/network-common.md#REQ-NET-API-BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE) · *Violated by:* [REQ-BR-NFT-BASE-CHAIN-PRIORITIES](network/bridge-networking.md#REQ-BR-NFT-BASE-CHAIN-PRIORITIES), [REQ-BR-NFT-IP-FORWARDING](network/bridge-networking.md#REQ-BR-NFT-IP-FORWARDING), [REQ-BR-NFT-MIGRATION](network/bridge-networking.md#REQ-BR-NFT-MIGRATION)

What a release does at the daemon's interfaces, later minor releases keep doing; a change needs a major release, or an option that restores the behavior. The daemon's interfaces are the Engine API, the CLI, the daemon's configuration, what these make observable in containers, networks and traffic, the anchors that a spec names, and behavior on a host that users observably rely on, which an observable requirement records. Everything else that the daemon creates on a host, such as its firewall rules, interfaces, namespaces and files, and their names, content and order, is how it brings that behavior about, and a minor release can change it.

<a id="PRIN-SECURITY-NOT-WEAKENED"></a>

**Principle PRIN-SECURITY-NOT-WEAKENED**: Security that a user enables is not weakened

*Refines:* [PRIN-STABLE](#PRIN-STABLE)

When a user enables a security feature, such as encryption of a network, a later minor release
does not give weaker protection. That includes the parameters that a security review of a
deployment records, such as the algorithms, the key lengths and the longest time that a key is
used. An option that restores the earlier protection does not make a weakening a minor-release
change. A major release that weakens one of them states it in its release notes.

<a id="PRIN-REPEATABLE"></a>

**Principle PRIN-REPEATABLE**: The outcome of a request does not depend on internal ordering

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAITHFUL](#PRIN-FAITHFUL) · *Violated by:* [BR-PUB-NO-SCTP-JOIN-ORDER](network/bridge-networking.md#BR-PUB-NO-SCTP-JOIN-ORDER), [NET-IFACE-NAME-COLLISION-ORDER](network/network-common.md#NET-IFACE-NAME-COLLISION-ORDER)

The outcome of a request depends only on the request and the state the daemon reports. The
daemon does not let an order it chooses internally, and that the request does not control,
decide whether the request succeeds.

<a id="PRIN-ERRORS-ACTIONABLE"></a>

**Principle PRIN-ERRORS-ACTIONABLE**: Errors say what to change

*Refines:* [PRIN-USER-INFORMED](#PRIN-USER-INFORMED) · *Violated by:* [BR-NOV6-V6-NETWORK-REFUSED-MSG](network/bridge-networking.md#BR-NOV6-V6-NETWORK-REFUSED-MSG), [BR-OPT-DAEMON-MTU-ERROR](network/bridge-networking.md#BR-OPT-DAEMON-MTU-ERROR), [BR-OPT-MTU-OUT-OF-RANGE](network/bridge-networking.md#BR-OPT-MTU-OUT-OF-RANGE), [NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-WRONG-KIND-MISREPORTED](network/network-common.md#NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-WRONG-KIND-MISREPORTED)

An error response, a task error or a log entry for a refused request, or for a failure that a
setting, option or object of the user causes, tells the user what to change: it names the
setting, option or object at fault and why, in the terms the user used. It does not report
internal state, such as a file path or a context deadline, in place of the cause.

<a id="PRIN-WARN-AHEAD"></a>

**Principle PRIN-WARN-AHEAD**: Foreseeable failures are reported when the request is accepted

*Refines:* [PRIN-USER-INFORMED](#PRIN-USER-INFORMED) · *Violated by:* [BR-ISO-NO-VETH-CONNECT](network/bridge-networking.md#BR-ISO-NO-VETH-CONNECT), [BR-ISO-NO-VETH-CREATE](network/bridge-networking.md#BR-ISO-NO-VETH-CREATE), [BR-PUB-NO-SCTP-CONNECT](network/bridge-networking.md#BR-PUB-NO-SCTP-CONNECT), [BR-PUB-NO-SCTP-CREATE](network/bridge-networking.md#BR-PUB-NO-SCTP-CREATE), [NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-START-FAILS](network/network-common.md#NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-START-FAILS), [NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-SWARM-START-FAILS](network/network-common.md#NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-SWARM-START-FAILS), [NET-API-CTR-CREATE-HOST-PORT-HELD](network/network-common.md#NET-API-CTR-CREATE-HOST-PORT-HELD), [NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-ADDRESS-CREATE](network/network-common.md#NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-ADDRESS-CREATE)

When a request is accepted with configuration that state the daemon holds will make a later
request, or the tasks of a service, fail, the daemon says so in that request's response, in its
warnings, not only when the later request or the tasks fail. That state can change before the
later request: whether an object exists, what holds a resource that the configuration asks for,
and the configuration of the daemon and the host. The user can then change the configuration or
the state. State that the daemon does not hold, such as the node-local networks of other nodes,
is not covered.
